Keywords: Tunis Maritime Custom and Genoa Pacts
RagShortTexts: The Hafsid dynasty ruled Tunis, where Muhammad al-Mustansir declared himself Caliph after.

Variants.Content: Ascending from Almohad governors in Ifriqiya, the Hafsid dynasty ruled Tunisia. Following the 1258 collapse of the Abbasid Caliphate in Baghdad, Sultan Muhammad I al-Mustansir claimed the supreme title of Commander of the Faithful (Caliph), briefly acknowledged across Mecca. Governing from Tunis, the dynasty regulated key Mediterranean maritime treaties.
Wealthy Hafsid customs drew Genoese and Venetian merchants, yet its strategic prominence placed Tunis directly into the crosshairs of King Louis IX's projected crusading fleets.
Christian cogs and corsair galleys moor peacefully in the Goletta lagoon. Paying dock dues to Hafsid bailiffs guarantees entry to bustling ivory, olive oil, and gold-dust bazaars.
